STRIKE_MECHANIC_DISCOVERED_2026-08-02.trigger: Given worm's confirmed stationary/anchored nature (no chase possible), the row's own 'missing' field named 'attack' as unresolved. The archived note's category description implies a proximity-triggered STRIKE (radius 700, contact ring dist^2 < ~200u per SYS_enemy_ai.md's generic aggro model) -- never live-tested for this species before.
STRIKE_MECHANIC_DISCOVERED_2026-08-02.method: Since the worm actively resists repositioning (see STATIONARY_ANCHORED_CONFIRMED), moved FLIK instead -- placed at the worm's own established (validated) Y, offset 400 units in X (well inside the documented 700-unit radius), using the pos+prev_pos+velocity method (all written together to avoid the game's own per-tick pos=prev+v integrator snapping Flik back, a lesson from the D09 audit). Sampled Flik's true health (0x800A6594) and the worm's own state every 5 frames immediately after placement.
STRIKE_MECHANIC_DISCOVERED_2026-08-02.result: Flik's HP dropped 4 -> 3 (one point of contact damage) within 5 frames of coming within 400 units. Simultaneously, Flik was propelled away at a steady, consistent velocity -- reaching over 12,000 units of separation within 30 frames. This EXPLAINS a repeated 'unexplained drift' observed in earlier attempts THIS session and in the D09/D13 work: it was not a bug or residual physics artifact, it was KNOCKBACK from the strike itself. The worm's own hp stayed exactly 8 throughout (the strike is not a mutual-damage contact). flags flipped 0x4045 -> 0x5045 (the same 0x1000 bit observed elsewhere, here clearly correlated with an active proximity/strike event) and vm_ip advanced through several addresses (0x80077a3a -> 0x80077a50 -> 0x80077a06 -> 0x80077a28), consistent with the mover-VM entering and completing its STRIKE bytecode section before returning to its normal wait loop. Only ONE strike landed -- the knockback carried Flik out of range before a second hit could occur.
STRIKE_MECHANIC_DISCOVERED_2026-08-02.conclusion: CONFIRMED: worm's proximity-triggered STRIKE deals 1 point of true-health contact damage to Flik and applies a strong knockback impulse, all within ~5 frames of coming inside roughly 400 units (well within the documented 700-unit radius). This is new, previously never live-tested behavior for this row -- the archived note only established the STRIKE opcode's existence and the radius operand statically, never its actual damage amount or the knockback side effect.

STRIKE_MECHANISM_STATIC_TRACE_2026-08-02.trigger: Operator asked whether the STRIKE mechanic was worth digging into at the ASM level. Checked already-decoded static data first (analysis/vm_programs.md) rather than starting a fresh MIPS disassembly hunt, per this session's own track record: the D09 berry-tough gate PC was found fast, the D13 one was a genuine time sink and was deprioritized -- so the honest move is to look for a cheap static answer before committing to a fresh search.
STRIKE_MECHANISM_STATIC_TRACE_2026-08-02.method: Read the full bytecode window around the vm_ip addresses observed live during the strike (analysis/vm_programs.md:392-411), then followed the call_native operand into the existing static census (analysis/functions.json, analysis/phase3_call_graph.json) and an ALREADY-DECOMPILED source file for that native.
STRIKE_MECHANISM_STATIC_TRACE_2026-08-02.bytecode_trace: 0x80077a08 player_proximity[700] (R=700) -> 0x80077a0c branch_if_s3[3] (taken when in range) -> 0x80077a14 flags_mask[63295,64] (sets flags+0x5c bit 0x40) -> 0x80077a1a call_native[8] -> native 0x80057b84 -> 0x80077a1e anim_clip_load[1,13] -> 0x80077a24 wait[13] -> 0x80077a28 park_arrive_stop. A SECOND, near-identical sequence exists later in the same worm program: 0x80077a70 player_proximity[1200] (larger radius) -> ... -> 0x80077a7c flags_mask[...,64] -> 0x80077a82 call_native[8] -> native 0x80057b84 again -- the worm's wander cycle has (at least) two proximity-strike windows, a smaller-radius one and a larger-radius one, both routed through the same native.
STRIKE_MECHANISM_STATIC_TRACE_2026-08-02.native_identity: 0x80057b84 is ALREADY named and decompiled in this repo: src/main/80057b84_vm_native_aimed_drop_spawn.c (documentation-grade, not byte-matched), backed by asm/hand_written/80057b84_sub_80057b84.s. The call graph (analysis/phase3_call_graph.json, key resident:resident:0x80057b84) shows exactly ONE caller, 0x8004c644 -- the mover-VM's own call_native opcode dispatcher -- consistent with reaching it only via this bytecode op, not a second independent path.
STRIKE_MECHANISM_STATIC_TRACE_2026-08-02.native_behavior: vm_native_aimed_drop_spawn(int *p): loops 8 times calling spawn_drop(p[1],p[2],p[3], 21+cycle(0..2), 6) -- the SAME spawn_drop (0x80059e44) used elsewhere for gold-berry/pickup drops (see gold-berry-drop mod memory) -- placing a burst of 8 objects cycling kinds 21/22/23 at the CALLER'S OWN position (the worm's own p[1..3], not Flik's). Then plays sound id 24. Then sets the spawned burst's facing (p[5]): if p[0]==40 (worm, HARD-CODED id check) it computes an atan2-style heading toward the player via sub_80060ae4((worm_x-player_x)>>5, (worm_z-player_z)>>5) and stores (angle+2048)&0xfff -- i.e. AIMED specifically at Flik's position at the moment of the call. For any other caller id, facing instead comes from a per-object descriptor byte (p[32] table), not aimed at the player at all.
STRIKE_MECHANISM_STATIC_TRACE_2026-08-02.interpretation: The STRIKE is NOT a direct body/contact-vs-actor hit going through contact_vs_actor_handler (0x80058AF8, the function searched twice already this session for the berry-tough gate PC and found more tangled than expected both times). It is a DIFFERENT code path: the mover-VM spawns a burst of 8 drop-type objects (kinds 21/22/23) at the worm's own position and aims that burst at Flik specifically because the caller's id is hard-coded as 40 in shared native code. The observed 1-point true-health hit + knockback almost certainly comes from Flik's own contact with one or more of those spawned objects after they are launched, not from the worm's own actor record directly.
STRIKE_MECHANISM_STATIC_TRACE_2026-08-02.residuals: NOT traced this pass: (1) the actual projectile/travel behavior of the spawned kind-21/22/23 objects and the exact handler that applies contact damage + knockback to Flik once one connects -- would need a fresh contact-pool watch on newly-spawned kind 21/22/23 records during a live strike; (2) kinds 21/22/23's own visual/render identity -- analysis/phase3_render_descriptors.json's table is keyed by counts in this dump, not directly indexable per-kind with the quick approach tried, so this needs a different static tool or a live gpu.pickObject/VRAM capture during an actual strike; (3) whether the 700-unit and 1200-unit windows produce observably different behavior (e.g. one arm/telegraph vs one strike) was not distinguished live.
STRIKE_MECHANISM_STATIC_TRACE_2026-08-02.conclusion: Cheap static win, no fresh disassembly required: the exact code path from proximity-trigger to native call is now fully traced and the native itself was ALREADY decompiled in this repo under a name that (in hindsight) directly matches what was observed live -- 'aimed drop spawn'. This is a materially better outcome than the two prior exact-PC searches this session; the remaining open question (how the spawned objects actually damage Flik) is a new, narrower, and separately-tractable follow-up, not the same open-ended tangle the berry-tough gate searches ran into.

strike_test_NEGATIVE.method: Same method as worm's own strike test: moved Flik (pos+prev_pos+velocity written atomically) to a fixed distance from wall_worm's own anchor (0x28/2c/30), using its own validated Y. Tested at TWO distances on two separate reloads: 400 units (dist^2=160000, well inside both the 700 and 1200 unit proximity-check radii) watched for 400 frames across 2 full wander-loop cycles, then 80 units (dist^2=6400, near point-blank) watched for 600 frames across ~2.5 loop cycles. Sampled Flik's true health (0x800A6594), position, and wall_worm's own hp/flags/vm_ip every 10 frames.
strike_test_NEGATIVE.result: NO STRIKE at either distance, across a combined 1000 frames (~16.6s) and roughly 4.5 full cycles through the shared wander loop. Critically, vm_ip was directly observed AT the proximity-check instructions themselves during this window (0x80077a6e -> 0x80077a70 at the 80-unit test, +550f sample) and the very next sample had already advanced past the check to 0x80077a90 without taking the in-range branch (0x80077a7c/call_native never reached) -- i.e. the check was reached and evaluated FALSE despite Flik being well inside both documented radii. This rules out 'the loop just never got there' as an explanation; the proximity test itself is not firing true for this actor under these conditions.
strike_test_NEGATIVE.hypothesis_not_confirmed_live: Since both actors execute the identical bytecode addresses and the 700/1200 radii are baked-in literals (identical for both), the most likely explanation is that the check depends on something beyond simple XZ-distance-to-anchor that differs for wall_worm specifically -- e.g. its true render/hitbox position may not equal its +0x28 anchor field the way worm's does (plausible for an actor that spends part of its cycle embedded/retracted 'in a wall', matching its name), or an additional gating flag/state not visited during this window. NOT resolved live this pass -- named as the next hop rather than guessed at further.
strike_test_NEGATIVE.conclusion: CONFIRMED NEGATIVE, well-tested (not a fluke or an under-tested miss): wall_worm does NOT exhibit the worm's proximity STRIKE behavior under conditions that reliably trigger it for worm (which struck within ~30 frames under an equivalent 400-unit setup). This is a genuine behavioral divergence within the family despite identical shared bytecode -- directly answers the operator's original question (whether the id==40-hardcoded aim special-case in the native implies wall_worm behaves differently) with a stronger and more specific result than expected: not just un-aimed, but apparently non-triggering under the tested conditions.

RESPAWN_MECHANISM_2026-08-02.live_confirmation: Killed a fresh worm (blue x4, matching the established -2/hit shape), then had Flik walk away using REAL controller input (debugger.resume + emulator.pressButton{button:'left', seconds} + debugger.pause, not a position poke) far enough (reliably ~76,000+ units on two separate runs) and watched: hp reset to 8 (full), id stayed 40, flags and vm_ip returned to values consistent with a fresh spawn (vm_ip landed near 0x800779f0, close to the program's own start). Re-confirmed live for THREE species this same day: worm, Redbug (D09), and shell_bug (D13) -- all three respawn once Flik genuinely walks away and the game processes real movement.
RESPAWN_MECHANISM_2026-08-02.position_pokes_never_reproduce_it: Multiple independent attempts to reproduce the reset via direct memory writes to Flik's own pos/prev_pos/velocity fields all FAILED, even when: (a) a single one-time teleport was followed by 50 real seconds of continuous debugger.resume with no further writes; (b) the write was constructed to present a 'real' one-frame prev->current delta (prev_pos=near, pos=far, matching what a huge single-frame walk would look like); (c) many small per-frame position increments were written each frame via debugger.scatterWrite + emulator.advanceFrames{frames:1}, reaching over 111,000 units total. NONE of these triggered the reset. Only genuine continuous execution with real controller input ever did. Consistent with this project's known advanceFrames gotcha (movie.advanceToFrame does not drive frames through the same PumpMessages->poll->OnFrameDone path as real 60Hz play) -- the same class of gap likely applies here to whatever subsystem tracks this.
RESPAWN_MECHANISM_2026-08-02.asm_trace_the_reset_write: Armed accessLog.addWatch (type write) on the worm's own hp field (base+0x6e) BEFORE a real walk-away, then captured the exact write live: instruction 'sh v0, 0x6e(t0)' at PC 0x80049ca4 (containing instruction at 0x80049ca0), writing hp 0 -> 8.

RESPAWN_MECHANISM_2026-08-02.asm_trace_the_actual_reinit_routine: 0x80049c2c reinstantiates an actor directly from its own spawn-chunk template, dereferenced via the actor's own backlink field (+0x80, matching the already-documented runtime-record backlink): id from backlink+0xc, position X/Y/Z from backlink+0/4/8 each shifted left 5 (matching Enemy_spawn_architecture.md's documented 'record XYZ<<5' spawn-anchor law exactly), the mover-VM program pointer from a lookup into the 13-entry program table at 0x80077AF8 keyed by backlink+0xd (matching the program-table-index discovery already banked under D13's ID11_IDENTIFIED_2026-08-02), hp from backlink+0x10 (the write accessLog caught, 'sh v0,0x6e(t0)' at 0x80049ca4), and flags from backlink+0x12. This is a genuine from-scratch re-instantiation, not a state toggle -- consistent with why the revived worm's vm_ip landed near the program's own start (0x800779f0) rather than resuming wherever it died.
RESPAWN_MECHANISM_2026-08-02.asm_trace_the_death_side_timer_set: Separately, and still accurately: debugger.xrefsTo on 0x800498ac (the documented bitmask function) finds exactly 3 callers -- 0x80059340 (inside the death tail of contact_vs_actor_handler's descendant, called with a1=1 immediately at death, right after the hp=999 sentinel write and the vm_ip reset to *(0x80077b2c)); and two calls at 0x8004d618 (a1=1) and 0x8004d644 (a1=2) inside the per-actor per-frame update function described below. a1's bit-0 branch runs a per-species jump table keyed on (id-6), each case writing a DIFFERENT negative countdown constant into the actor's own +0x4a signed halfword (observed constants include -24, -33, -16, -25 for different id ranges; worm's own exact constant not yet isolated) before falling through to 'sh v0, 0x4a(s0)'. a1's bit-1 branch is the documented terminal-retirement path (clears hp/id, unrelated to the revival -- see CORRECTION above). Whether/how this timer or the a1=2 retirement path relate to triggering the SEPARATE reinit routine at 0x80049c2c (e.g. as a precondition, or as an entirely independent trigger) is NOT established -- named as an open question, not assumed.
RESPAWN_MECHANISM_2026-08-02.asm_trace_the_per_frame_timer_tick: The per-actor update function (functionStart 0x8004d224, functionEnd 0x8004d6a4, confidence exact) loops over the live actor-pointer table (0x80090748, 64 slots) each frame, ticking each entry's +0x4a countdown as described above. This timer mechanism is confirmed to exist and fire 0x800498ac(actor, 1 or 2) on crossing zero -- but its exact causal relationship to the reinit routine's execution (0x80049c2c) was NOT established live (see CALLER_NOT_CONFIRMED below). It is presented here as the most likely trigger given its timing and role, not as a confirmed link.
RESPAWN_MECHANISM_2026-08-02.CALLER_NOT_CONFIRMED: debugger.xrefsTo on 0x80049c2c finds ZERO static callers (no literal jal/j reaches it) -- it is invoked via an indirect/computed call (a function-pointer table entry or jalr), consistent with the per-species jump-table pattern seen elsewhere in this same file's death-tail code. An execTrace.addWatch armed on pc=0x80049c2c during a live walk-away-and-reset run captured ZERO hits even though the hp reset demonstrably fired in the same run (hp 0->8 confirmed at +60f) -- this is almost certainly a tooling/methodology gap (the SAME execTrace 0-hits-despite-real-event pattern was independently observed once already this session, in the wall_worm red-berry throw-dispatch check), not evidence the routine wasn't reached. The exact caller of 0x80049c2c, and therefore the precise trigger condition for the reinit itself, remains UNCONFIRMED.
RESPAWN_MECHANISM_2026-08-02.asm_trace_the_admission_check_UNRESOLVED: The per-frame function (0x8004d224) ALSO contains an earlier pass (0x8004d264-~0x8004d410) that scans the level's full static actor array and, for each entry, computes squared XZ-ish distance against a cached reference point (a fixed 12-byte struct at 0x8009ec50) versus a per-actor radius field, ADMITTING the actor into the live table (0x80090748) only when the distance check passes (near the reference point). xrefsTo on 0x8009ec50 finds exactly ONE writer, 0x8004ec94, inside a function (0x8004ea8c-0x8004ecd0) that populates it from the CAMERA's own tracked state (via 0x8004df18, already Canon-established elsewhere this campaign as camera_follow_update) in the normal case, or from the scripted setpiece actor (0x80090bc0-adjacent fields, via 0x8004dd98) in a special case. So the reference point is a camera-position proxy, not Flik's raw position -- a plausible reason position pokes never worked, since they never touch this separate cached struct. HOWEVER: read literally, admission requires being WITHIN the radius of that anchor, which would mean staying NEAR should tick the timer and walking FAR should freeze it -- the OPPOSITE of the confirmed live behavior. This contradiction is NOT resolved, and its relevance to the ACTUAL reinit routine (0x80049c2c, whose real trigger is separately unconfirmed per CALLER_NOT_CONFIRMED) is itself uncertain -- it may not even be the right code path to explain the reinit at all. Plausible unexamined explanations: the admission radius may be small enough that even the 'near' test position was already outside it; an hp-gate earlier in the function that changes which branch a dead actor takes was not located; a register misread in partial disassembly; or this admission check and the actual reinit trigger are unrelated systems entirely. NOT to be treated as confidently understood -- named explicitly as an open contradiction, not glossed over.

GRUB_IDENTITY_AND_FULL_ARMOR_SWEEP_2026-.method_breakthrough_pressButton_auto_pau: The prior pass's failure to land straight throws was NOT purely a facing/aim-cone problem -- part of it was a testing-method bug. emulator.pressButton with a 'seconds' duration auto-pauses the emulator internally once its own hold window elapses; a caller must issue a FRESH debugger.resume AFTER pressButton returns to let projectile travel time actually elapse, or all subsequent polling reads a frozen, paused game (confirmed live: the thrown-berry gate 0x800a6596 never changed across 4 continuous seconds of polling until this fix was applied, then it correctly showed the gate active for ~1s before resolving). This is a general method note, not specific to grub -- likely affects any live combat test in this project using pressButton with a manual post-press polling loop.
GRUB_IDENTITY_AND_FULL_ARMOR_SWEEP_2026-.method_breakthrough_facing: With the pressButton fix applied, straight (non-homing) throws still missed from the fixture's default orientation. A brief 'left' d-pad tap (0.15s) immediately before throwing turns Flik enough to connect reliably. Homing-type throws (green/marker2, already confirmed; mega/marker4, confirmed this pass) behave OPPOSITELY -- they must be thrown from the DEFAULT orientation WITHOUT the turn; adding the 'left' turn before a mega throw caused it to whiff even after a 5-second wait, while removing the turn and waiting ~1.0-1.5s let it connect and kill. This is consistent with homing using its own acquisition-based targeting (per the already-established distinction in EARTHWORM_ID12_SWEEP_2026-08-02) that a manual facing adjustment can apparently disrupt.

One naming caveat: marker value 0 was assumed to correspond to 'red' by elimination against the established kind-to-marker pickup table (0x21/22/23/24 = green/gold/blue/purple respectively, leaving 0x20/marker-0 as the remaining default/red slot) -- this specific mapping was not independently re-verified this pass, though the behavioral finding (every tested marker value connects) holds regardless of the exact class name for marker 0.

GRUB_AGGRO_2026-08-02.trigger: Follow-up pass, same day, closing 'grub's own aggro/chase behavior beyond the static no-strike-opcode finding' from STILL_OPEN.
GRUB_AGGRO_2026-08-02.method: hp=1 makes a single hit lethal, so a test-only HP poke (writeU16, actor+0x6e, 1 -> 8) was applied BEFORE the hit to let the actor survive and be observed post-hit -- flagged explicitly as a test intervention, not natural gameplay, same as other poke-based mechanism tests in this project. Landed one throw (marker 0, 'left'-turn method from GRUB_IDENTITY_AND_FULL_ARMOR_SWEEP_2026-08-02), then polled position (+0x04/08/0c) and flags (+0x5c) against Flik's stationary position for ~6 real seconds (debugger.resume + 0.3s poll steps).
GRUB_AGGRO_2026-08-02.result: The CHASE bit (flags+0x5c bit 0x2) sets on the hit (0x4001 -> 0x4003), matching the same mechanism already confirmed for Redbug, shell_bug, and mite. Unlike shell_bug/mite (bit sets, no real movement), grub's position traces a genuine APPROACH-THEN-RETREAT ARC: distance to Flik falls from 15883 units at the hit to a minimum of ~4856 units around t=3.0-3.3s, then rises again to 21657 by t=5.7s. This is the same 'approach/retreat stand-off oscillation' shape already documented for D09 Redbug, not a monotonic charge to contact. A second flag transition (0x4003 -> 0x5001, losing bit 0x2, gaining bit 0x1000) occurs partway through the arc (~t=1.2s) while the approach-then-retreat motion continues uninterrupted -- the persistent movement-driving state is more likely tied to 0x1000 than to the initial-hit bit 0x2, not confirmed further this pass.
GRUB_AGGRO_2026-08-02.conclusion: Grub DOES chase -- a genuine behavioral divergence from mite (CONFIRMED NEGATIVE, see analysis/phase4_d11_mite.json's AGGRO_2026-08-02) and from shell_bug, despite all three sharing the same CHASE-bit-sets-on-hit mechanism. Closes 'grub's own aggro/chase behavior' from STILL_OPEN.
